chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I complain to you about what I experience of whispers (waswasa) in my prayer, to the extent that I do not know whether I have prayed with increase or decrease.'
So he said: 'When you enter into your prayer, strike your left thigh with your right forefinger (which is reciting/tasbih), then say:
'In the name of Allah, and by Allah I rely upon Allah. I seek refuge with Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the Pelted Satan.'
For indeed you slaughter him and repel him.

key_terms.الْمُسَبِّحَة: The forefinger used for tasbih (counting prayers)
key_terms.الْوَسْوَسَة: Whispers or doubts (specifically from Satan) that cause uncertainty during worship
key_terms.تَنْحَرُهُ: You slaughter him (metaphorically defeating the source of doubt)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed remedy for doubt and whispers (waswasa) during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the specific issue of persistent doubt (waswasa) that disrupts the certainty of prayer, offering a physical and verbal remedy to anchor the worshipper's focus. The instruction to strike the thigh while reciting the supplication serves as a tangible method to 'slaughter' the whispers of Satan, reflecting the Shia emphasis on combining spiritual reliance with practical discipline. This guidance is particularly significant for those whose doubts are frequent enough to obscure the count of rak'ats, distinguishing it from minor, fleeting doubts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to the Prophetsaww and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! I complain to you of what I face from the uncertainty during my Salāt to the extent that I do not know what I prayed from an increase or decrease’.
So hesaww said: ‘When you enter into your Salāt, so stab your left thigh with your right forefinger, then say,

‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. I rely upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. I seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the Pelted Satan<sup>la</sup>’,
So you would slaughter him<sup>la</sup> and repel him<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Once a man came to the Holy prophet, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I complain before you against misgivings I face in my Salah (prayer) so much so that I do not know how much I have performed, increased or decreased.
He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘When you begin your Salah (prayer) hit your left thigh with your right forefinger and say, ‘
In the name of Allah, I choose Allah, the all-knowing and all-hearing as my attorney against Satan, condemned to be stoned,
thus, you slaughter and repel him.’”
